summaries: • 3IINFOLTD (Order Book): 3i Infotech Limited has secured a significant three-year purchase order valued at Rs. 24.48 Crore (exclusive of taxes) from a new banking institution in India, commencing January 1, 2027. This contract, providing comprehensive IT Facility Management Services and related infrastructure support, positively impacts future revenue visibility and expands the company's domestic client base. The only notable point is the non-disclosure of the new customer's name, explicitly stated due to confidentiality obligations. └ 📄 Source

• AARVI (Insider Trades): Aarvi Encon Limited has informed stock exchanges about an upcoming video conference investor meet on November 27, 2026, where a Key Managerial Person will discuss publicly available information with a group of investors. The company explicitly states that no unpublished price sensitive information (UPSI) is intended to be shared, mitigating risks of selective disclosure. This is a routine investor relations compliance disclosure with no apparent immediate material impacts or red flags. └ 📄 Source

• ABDL (Order Book): Executive Summary: Allied Blenders and Distillers Limited (ABDL) is appealing a sole arbitrator's decision that terminated arbitration proceedings against the Canteen Stores Department (CSD) concerning disputed debit notes and recoveries for whisky supplies. A significant red flag is the arbitrator's finding that no arbitration agreement existed, which could ultimately prevent ABDL from recovering potentially material amounts if their High Court appeal fails. This development prolongs the dispute, incurring further legal costs with an uncertain financial outcome for the company. └ 📄 Source

• ADANIENSOL (Presentations & PR): Adani Energy Solutions (AESL) has secured a significant Bihar transmission project through competitive bidding, projected to generate an annual tariff of approximately Rs 500 crore upon its commissioning by late 2028. This project materially expands AESL's portfolio by adding 881 circuit kilometers of transmission lines and 3,160 MVA of transformation capacity, bolstering the state's grid while specifically evacuating 2,400 MW from an upcoming Adani Power plant. While competitively bid, the notable aspect is the intra-group synergy for power evacuation. └ 📄 Source

• ADVENZYMES (Major Deals): Advanced Enzyme Technologies Limited (AETL) has acquired an additional 1.22% stake in its subsidiary, JC Biotech Private Limited (JCB), for ₹22.80 million, increasing its total ownership to 96.94%. This transaction is a step towards making JCB a Wholly Owned Subsidiary, with AETL actively pursuing the remaining 3.06% equity. The acquisition reflects a strategic move to consolidate control and simplify the corporate structure, with no apparent red flags. └ 📄 Source

• AGARWALEYE (Major Deals): Dr. Agarwal's Health Care Limited has completed its amalgamation with Dr. Agarwal's Eye Hospital Limited, issuing 1,51,90,373 new equity shares to the former's eligible shareholders as part of the scheme. This corporate action significantly increases the company's paid-up equity share capital by approximately 4.79%, resulting in dilution for existing shareholders but marking a key step in integrating the two entities. No immediate red flags are present, as this filing confirms the execution of a previously announced merger plan. └ 📄 Source

• AHCL (Regulatory Risk): Executive Summary: Anlon Healthcare Limited has announced an analyst/investor meeting scheduled for November 27, 2026, to engage with the investment community. The company explicitly states that discussions will be based solely on publicly available information, ensuring no Unpublished Price Sensitive Information (UPSI) will be disclosed, which is a standard regulatory compliance measure. This appears to be a routine investor relations activity with no immediate material financial impact or red flags identified. └ 📄 Source

• AHLUCONT (Concalls): Ahluwalia Contracts (India) Ltd. reported a significant sequential recovery in 2QFY27 turnover and PAT, offsetting a weak Q1, but half-year profitability and EBITDA margins still show a material year-on-year decline. Key headwinds include anticipated Q3 revenue impact from recurring NCR pollution shutdowns (partially mitigated by the exempt Central Vista project) and a persistently delayed Mumbai Gems & Jewellery Park project, suggesting continued pressure on execution and profitability despite a robust order book and positive revenue guidance. └ 📄 Source

• ALKEM (Regulatory Risk): Alkem Laboratories Limited has received a US FDA warning letter for its Amaliya, Daman manufacturing facility, an escalation from its previously classified "Official Action Indicated (OAI)" status. While the company states there is no material impact on current operations or financials and they continue to supply approved products to the U.S. market, a warning letter is a significant regulatory red flag that typically requires substantial corrective actions and could pose future risks to product approvals and sales if deficiencies are not adequately addressed. └ 📄 Source

• AMBER (Concalls): Amber Enterprises India Limited reported strong H1 FY27 revenue growth (+28% YoY), driven by explosive 94% growth in its Electronics Division and robust 41% growth in Consumer Durables, but faced significant profitability challenges with an adjusted loss in Q2 and a material exceptional loss of INR 132.2 crores in H1. Key material impacts include severe margin pressure across both the Consumer Durables and Railways divisions due to commodity inflation, currency fluctuations, and fixed-price contracts. While management projects these margin pressures are temporary and expects a rebound from Q2 FY28 for Railways, the company's high net debt of INR 2,582 crores and planned capex of up to INR 2,000 crores are notable, even as it diversifies into mobile manufacturing. └ 📄 Source
